# `aitbc exchange order fund`

Fund an unfunded SELL order with its AIT escrow lock. Reads the funding instruction from my-orders (escrow address, required AIT, sell_quote payload) and sends the lock TRANSFER from this node's own wallet — the sender must be the order owner (stranger locks are refunded, never credited). --print emits the equivalent 'transactions send' line without broadcasting anything. Operator note (CLI-1/CLI-4): the password path was fixed after the 15 Oct D1 find — the loader's resolution is replaced by a plaintext address read plus a single password resolution reused for the send, covered by a real encrypted-wallet test. The command has still never broadcast live — a real transfer is an AIT move the operator names explicitly.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc exchange order fund [OPTIONS] ORDER_ID
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `order_id` | integer | yes | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--fee` | decimal | `0.01` | no | AIT chain fee for the lock transfer (standard chain fee) |
| `--print` | flag | `false` | no | Emit the equivalent 'transactions send' line; broadcast nothing |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet name (not a file path) — must be the order owner's |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL for the lock transfer |
| `--exchange-url` | text | — | no | Override exchange service base URL |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc exchange order fund ORDER_ID
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc exchange order fund ORDER_ID --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
